name: M6.4C controlled self-correction cases
label_status: PROVISIONAL: labels and expected interpretations were written by the assistant (Claude Code) from the policy text in data/documents/. No human has reviewed them yet. They are not Gemini output and not V3 output.
answer_provenance_note: Every original answer below was supplied by the evaluation, not generated by Gemini. Answers marked seeded_error contain a deliberately introduced error; they are NOT organic Gemini mistakes. Answers adapted from the M5 benchmark reuse that benchmark's claim (exploratory material only). The live-run case reuses the claim wording reported from the first live M6.4A run; its question and evidence snapshot were re-created here because that run's output was not saved.
evidence: Each case's evidence snapshot is frozen at build time from the production retrieval pipeline (hybrid, dense 0.6 / BM25 0.4, top 5) for the case question. Excerpts must be exact substrings of a snapshot section.

cases.question: How long do domestic customers have to request a refund?
cases.original_answer: Domestic customers may request a refund within 14 days of delivery.
cases.provenance_note: Seeded error: the 30-day domestic window was changed to 14 days.

expected.interpretation: Domestic customers may request a refund within 30 days of delivery; 14 days is wrong.
expected.ideal_correction: State the 30-day window (of delivery) and cite REF-728.1.

statements.statement: Domestic customers may request a refund within 14 days of delivery.
statements.label: factually_incorrect
statements.excerpt: may request a refund within 30 days of delivery

cases.question: What is the hotel cap for business travel?
cases.original_answer: Hotel stays for business travel are capped at $200 per night in standard locations.
cases.provenance_note: Seeded error: the $250 standard-location cap was changed to $200.

expected.interpretation: The cap is $250 per night in standard locations ($350 in designated high-cost cities).
expected.ideal_correction: State $250 per night in standard locations; $350 in high-cost cities may be added.

statements.statement: Hotel stays are capped at $200 per night in standard locations.
statements.label: factually_incorrect
statements.excerpt: Hotel stays are capped at $250 per night in standard locations and $350 per night in designated high-cost cities.

cases.question: Do unused paid learning days carry over to the next year?
cases.original_answer: Employees receive 3 paid learning days per year that may be used for approved training. Unused paid learning days carry over to the next year.
cases.provenance_note: Adapted from M5 benchmark V033 (exploratory). The second sentence is a seeded unsupported claim: the evidence says the unused allowance (money) does not carry over and says nothing about learning days.

expected.interpretation: 3 paid learning days per year is stated; whether unused learning days carry over is not stated.
expected.ideal_correction: Keep the 3 learning days; remove the carry-over claim or say the policy does not address it (without claiming they do not carry over).

statements.statement: Employees receive 3 paid learning days per year that may be used for approved training.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Employees also receive 3 paid learning days per year that may be used for approved training.

statements.statement: Unused paid learning days carry over to the next year.
statements.label: insufficient_evidence
statements.excerpt: Unused allowance does not carry over to the next year.

cases.question: How long is the warranty on company-branded hardware?
cases.original_answer: Company-branded hardware products include a 2-year limited warranty from the date of delivery. Customers can extend the warranty to 3 years by purchasing an extended protection plan.
cases.provenance_note: Seeded unsupported claim: no section mentions an extended protection plan or a 3-year warranty.

expected.interpretation: The 2-year limited warranty from delivery is stated; an extension to 3 years is not mentioned anywhere.
expected.ideal_correction: Keep the 2-year warranty; remove the extension claim.

statements.statement: Company-branded hardware products include a 2-year limited warranty from the date of delivery.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Company-branded hardware products include a 2-year limited warranty from the date of delivery

statements.statement: Customers can extend the warranty to 3 years by purchasing an extended protection plan.
statements.label: insufficient_evidence
statements.excerpt: Accessories such as cables, cases, and chargers include a 1-year limited warranty.

cases.question: What is the standard refund window for domestic customers?
cases.original_answer: For domestic customers, the standard refund window is within 30 days of delivery.
cases.provenance_note: Claim wording (C1) from the first live M6.4A run, where V3 marked it conflicting_evidence because REF-728.3 (refund processing time) was read as a contradiction. The question and snapshot are re-created; the live run's original answer text was not saved. The answer is correct.

expected.interpretation: Correct: 30 days of delivery. REF-728.3's 5 business days concerns refund processing, a different event.
expected.ideal_correction: No change needed; a correction should keep the 30-day window.

statements.statement: For domestic customers, the standard refund window is within 30 days of delivery.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: may request a refund within 30 days of delivery

cases.question: Do I need meal receipts when claiming per diem?
cases.original_answer: Meal receipts are not required for per diem claims.
cases.provenance_note: Adapted from M5 benchmark V032, where V3 falsely read the general receipt rule (FIN-201.4) as a contradiction. The answer is correct.

expected.interpretation: Correct: per diem replaces itemized meal receipts. FIN-201.4's receipt rule covers airfare, accommodation, transport and items above $25, not per diem meals.

statements.statement: Meal receipts are not required for per diem claims.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: meal receipts are not required for per diem claims

cases.question: How are domestic refunds processed and is there a restocking fee?
cases.original_answer: Domestic refunds are issued to the original payment method within 5 business days after the returned item is received and inspected, and opened electronics are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.
cases.provenance_note: Correct but compound: two facts in one sentence.

expected.interpretation: Both facts are stated in REF-728.3.
expected.ideal_correction: No factual change; splitting into two sentences is acceptable.

statements.statement: Domestic refunds are issued to the original payment method within 5 business days after the returned item is received and inspected.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Domestic refunds are issued to the original payment method within 5 business days after the returned item is received and inspected.

statements.statement: Opened electronics are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Opened electronics are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.

cases.question: Do employees have to repay tuition assistance if they leave?
cases.original_answer: Employees who resign within 12 months of receiving tuition assistance must repay 100 percent of the amount and employees who resign between 12 and 24 months must repay 50 percent, but repayment does not apply when employment ends due to redundancy.
cases.provenance_note: Correct but compound: three facts in one sentence.

expected.interpretation: All three rules are stated in HR-105.3.
expected.ideal_correction: No factual change; splitting is acceptable.

statements.statement: Employees who resign within 12 months of receiving tuition assistance must repay 100 percent of the amount.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Employees who resign within 12 months of receiving tuition assistance or certification funding must repay 100 percent of the amount

statements.statement: Employees who resign between 12 and 24 months must repay 50 percent.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: employees who resign between 12 and 24 months must repay 50 percent

statements.statement: Repayment does not apply when employment ends due to redundancy.
statements.label: factually_supported
statements.excerpt: Repayment does not apply when employment ends due to redundancy.

statements.statement: A domestic package may be reported lost if it has not arrived 10 business days after the estimated delivery date.

statements.excerpt: A domestic package may be reported lost if it has not arrived 10 business days after the estimated delivery date.

cases.question: What is the first-response target for P2 support cases?
cases.original_answer: P2 support cases have a first-response target of 1 hour.
cases.provenance_note: Adapted from M5 benchmark V026, where V3 wrongly accepted it. Seeded entity confusion: 1 hour is the P1 target.

expected.interpretation: P2's first-response target is 4 business hours; 1 hour belongs to P1.

statements.statement: P2 support cases have a first-response target of 1 hour.
statements.label: factually_incorrect
statements.excerpt: P2 cases involve major functionality loss with no workaround and have a first-response target of 4 business hours.

cases.question: Can I get a full refund if I cancel my annual subscription?
cases.original_answer: Customers on annual plans may cancel within 30 days of the initial purchase and receive a full refund.
cases.provenance_note: Adapted from M5 benchmark V039, where V3 wrongly accepted it. Seeded number confusion: 30 days is the renewal-reminder lead time; the cooling-off period is 14 days.

expected.interpretation: Full refund only within 14 days of the initial purchase or of an annual renewal.
expected.ideal_correction: State the 14-day window (initial purchase or annual renewal).

statements.statement: Customers on annual plans may cancel within 30 days of the initial purchase and receive a full refund.
statements.label: factually_incorrect
statements.excerpt: Customers on annual plans may cancel within 14 days of the initial purchase or of an annual renewal and receive a full refund.
